Actor Prakash Raj speaking at a press conference at DYFI office in Mangaluru on Saturday. | Photo Credit: H.S. MANJUNATH
Actor Prakash Raj said that, in order to save the right of voters to cast their franchise, he is joining the Chalo Dilli march, organised by several organisations and led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, in New Delhi on Sunday.
“Earlier, I was part of the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which was organised by Cockroach Janata Party. For me, the nation comes first. Its [Chalo Dilli march] cause is to save the country. Hence, I am taking part in the programme for which Rahul Gandhi has taken the lead,” he said.
Asking the Congress-led State government to take a tough stance over the deletion of nearly one crore voters in the State, the actor said he was dismayed over the inaction of MPs, MLAs, and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar over the deletion of voters from the final electoral roll after the three-month-long Special Intensive Revision.
Raising questions over the large number of deletions in the State, Mr. Raj said that, in addition to the deletion of dead and double entries, over 70 lakh voters have been deleted on account of being absent and permanently shifted. In Bengaluru City alone, over 50% of voters have been deleted, and the total number of voters has been brought down to 53 lakh.
Mr. Raj said his own name has been deleted in Bengaluru on the ground of being “permanently shifted”. “I have moved to a house three lanes away from the place it was in 2002. Election officials asked me to file Form 6 for the inclusion of my name, and they have barred me from filing Form 8 for the shift of name. I will not file Form 6 with a false declaration that I have not voted earlier. I will take legal recourse (for the voting right),” he said.
The actor said he travelled across the State and spoke to several social activists during the SIR. He was the first to discover the bulk filing of Form 7 for the deletion of voters. Action should have been taken against the attempt to delete a section of voters belonging to minority communities, tribals, Scheduled Castes, and other gullible voters. As against claims made by the BJP that the SIR was for deleting a large number of Bangladeshis and Pakistanis from the electoral roll, only a couple of Bangladeshi and Pakistani women were deleted in Karnataka.
Asked about the relevance of agitations against the SIR when the Supreme Court was hearing the issue, the actor spoke of the pain that voters have endured during the SIR. “We have every right to express our anguish over the (SIR) process,” he said.
